blocks.text: Specific heat is a property of the material: doubling the mass doubles heat capacity, not c. Convert litres: 1 L = 10⁻³ m³.

items: Heat given out → Q negative. Work done ON gas → W negative.

blocks.text: Heat at constant pressure: Q = nCpΔT. Work part = nRΔT, e.g. 2 mol, ΔT 50 K → W = 2 × 8.3 × 50 = 830 J.

title: PN junction: forward vs reverse bias

blocks.text: Depletion region: no free carriers, only fixed ions — negative ions on the p-side, positive ions on the n-side. Barrier: Si ≈ 0.7 V, Ge ≈ 0.3 V.
Majority carriers: holes in p-type, electrons in n-type.
A Si diode conducts only above 0.7 V. With 0.4 V forward, current ≈ 0. In a circuit: I = (V − 0.7)/R, e.g. (5.7 − 0.7)/1 kΩ = 5 mA.

items: E = hf = hc/λ

1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (divide J by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ to get eV)
Power P = n·hf, so photons per second n = P/hf

blocks.text: Light comes in packets (photons). Higher f / shorter λ → more energy per photon: violet > red, X-ray > UV > visible > IR.
E ∝ 1/λ, not λ. Halve the wavelength → energy doubles. Brighter light means more photons, not more energetic photons.

f₀ = threshold frequency: below it, no electrons at any intensity

Graph K.E.max vs f: straight line, slope = h, x-intercept = f₀

blocks.text: Quick sum: 5 eV photon on a 2 eV metal → K.E.max = 3 eV. The effect proves light behaves as particles.

items: Emission: hf = E_upper − E_lower = ΔE
λ = hc/ΔE (bigger gap → shorter λ)
Ionisation from ground state = 13.6 eV
Lines possible from level n down to ground: n(n − 1)/2

blocks.text: Levels are fixed (quantised), so only certain photon energies appear → line spectrum, unique for each element. Negative energy means the electron is bound (zero = free).
−3.4 → −13.6 eV gives a 10.2 eV photon. An atom absorbs only photons that exactly match a gap (e.g. 10.2 eV or 12.09 eV from ground).

blocks.text: The series is named by the LOWER level the electron falls to. The first Balmer line (red, 656 nm) is n = 3 → 2. n = 5 → 3 is Paschen.
Longest λ in a series = smallest jump (Lyman: 2 → 1). Shortest λ (highest energy) in a series = series limit, ∞ → lower level (Lyman: ∞ → 1, 13.6 eV).
